subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning the vehicle structure as a single TypeScript module, using a static hull with a few joints for turret yaw, gun elevation, and stabiliser legs, keeping bone placement explicit but moderate in complexity.

For dimensions, I'm sketching a roughly 9m hull with three wheel axles per side, each wheel built from a cylinder hub plus small lug-nut details, and four corner outriggers extending sideways as stabiliser legs.

For the stabiliser legs, I'll build rod connections from hull joints out to ground pads at y=0, matching the wheel contact height so everything rests flush on the floor.

For the railgun, I'm planning a rear-mounted turret with two parallel rails extending forward, elevated about 20 degrees, computed along a direction vector from the pivot point.

Now I'm orienting each gun part's box geometry along the aim direction using a "dir" and axis setting so components stack correctly down the barrel length, and planning to add glow effects from the kit for the capacitor coils, rail interior, headlights, and cockpit glass, plus decal textures for hazard stripes, insignia, and cockpit windows. For paint, I'm thinking through a mottled olive/dark green/tan camo pattern with metal grain and countershading.

I'm picking a color palette of olive, dark green, tan, steel, gunmetal, black, orange, and cyan, then blocking out the hull as stacked boxes for the lower hull, upper deck, and cab, with the cab's sloped glacis plate built using an extruded side profile.

I'm computing the normal direction for the windshield slant plane and sizing the glow decal, then skipping side windows and considering simple mudguard boxes above the wheels to suggest fenders.

Now I'm positioning the wheel fenders outside the hull, adding axle rods and suspension arms connecting hull to wheels, then starting the turret ring and turret base on top of the upper deck.

For the turret I'm shaping an octagonal base cylinder with a joint for yaw rotation and a gun joint for aim direction, then building a railgun with twin side rails, periodic spacer bands, flank-mounted capacitor coils, a muzzle brake ring, and a glowing cyan strip between the rails with coil rings for extra detail.

Now I'm moving to the rear turret details—cooling box, ammo rack, antenna rods—then designing stabilizer legs: outrigger beams from the hull sides extending to hydraulic pistons with sleeves and octagonal pads, plus diagonal braces for structural support.

I'm positioning the legs at z=±3.7 so they clear the wheel radius at 2.8, deciding four legs is sufficient without a middle pair, and now setting up the joint hierarchy—hull root, turret, gun, four legs, and six wheel joints.

Now I'm designing a part helper function to streamline creating geometry with color, bone, position, and options, then figuring out how to build the tire: a faceted cylinder for the tire body, and considering whether to add tread detail using multiple small boxes per wheel or simplify with just a textured cylinder and paint stripes instead.

Still working out tread block rotation math...

Now I'm thinking about hull decals: positioning insignia, roundels, and stripe markings as textured planes on the sides, plus a serial number label like "RG-06", while considering mirroring issues for the opposite side.

Still writing camo texture code...

I'm planning more surface details: a roundel decal, glassy window reflections, glowing warm headlights, a "DANGER HV" warning label on the turret, a radar dish on the mast, and smoke grenade launcher tubes mounted on the turret sides. Then I'm setting up a coordinate helper for positioning gun-local points relative to the elevation pivot, using direction and up vectors to place barrel-mounted geometry.

Writing box and cylinder helpers...

Now I'm structuring the skeleton -- a turret joint on the hull and a railgun joint parented to the turret at the elevation pivot -- then building the lower hull as an extruded wedge profile for the wedge nose shape, keeping the cab as a separate piece.

I'll use an extruded chassis colored in camo instead of a plain box, then add a rear ammo/power module with vents, two exhaust stacks at the rear corners, a front hazard bumper plane, and glowing headlight boxes near the nose while skipping tow hooks for now.

I'm checking wheel positions and gaps to figure out where side equipment boxes can fit between the wheels without clipping, working out the x and z ranges so the olive-colored tool boxes sit cleanly in the open space.

Now I'm setting up suspension rods connecting the hull to each wheel center with steel cylinders, plus axle housing at the hubs, then moving into writing the actual build code with imports, joints, and the distinct color constraints in mind. Writing joint setup code...

Now I'm adding the radar mast and dish using a lathe profile with a tilted axis, then setting up the glow effect calls on the parts.
